info.title: LoonFS HTTP API
info.description: Static OpenAPI document for the LoonFS v0 HTTP API.

get.description: Returns `ok` when the server is running and can accept requests.

Returns `ready` while the server admits new work. Once shutdown begins and publisher admission closes, answers 503 `shutting_down` so load balancers can drain the instance. `/health` stays the liveness probe: it only reports that the process is up.

503.description: Shutdown has begun; admission is closed

post.description: Creates a named, user-owned checkpoint record pinning the current namespace view. Every call mints a new record under a new id; the name is a label, not a key. The record is a garbage-collection root until it is released, so routine maintenance should flush the WAL instead. This is a maintenance/admin operation, not a file mutation.

400.description: Invalid namespace id, name, or lifetime

post.description: Releases a user-owned checkpoint pin by id. Idempotent: releasing an already-released or reaped record succeeds. The record is reaped by a later garbage-collection pass; its pinned data becomes collectable only on the pass after that.

400.description: Invalid id, or the checkpoint is fork-owned

post.description: Disables the namespace's grep root, clears its segment references, and stops its embedded driver. Explicit grep garbage collection later reclaims the segments. Idempotent.

200.description: Grep root disabled or already disabled

403.description: The backing store rejected its configured credentials

409.description: Lost a grep root-pointer publication race; retry

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: Grep serving is disabled for this deployment

post.description: Enables the namespace's grep root. Embedded mode immediately starts that namespace's event-driven backfill driver; serve-only deployments rely on their explicitly assigned external driver. Idempotent.

200.description: Grep root enabled or already enabled

403.description: The backing store rejected its configured credentials

409.description: Lost a grep root-pointer publication race; retry

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: Grep serving is disabled for this deployment

post.description: Runs one explicit garbage-collection pass over only this namespace's grep-owned extension keyspace. A tombstoned or absent namespace has aged extension state reaped; no grep garbage collection runs implicitly.

403.description: The backing store rejected its configured credentials

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: Grep serving is disabled for this deployment

post.description: Runs one bounded maintenance step: flushes the WAL tail once it reaches the threshold, and optionally runs a garbage-collection pass afterwards. Step-driven GC defaults to 1024 candidates and returns its cursor for a later step rather than looping internally. Losing the root race is an outcome, not an error.

get.description: Returns a summary of supported features and limits.

409.description: Namespace already exists or is partial

410.description: Namespace id was deleted and retired

get.description: Returns the current head, manifest, checkpoint, WAL tail, and retention state for a namespace.

parameters.name: expected_head_seq
parameters.description: Delete only if the namespace head is still at this sequence

get.description: Returns committed changes from the write-ahead log. Callers can use this feed to keep another projection synchronized with WAL history.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Return committed changes after this sequence

post.description: Applies one commit: an ordered, non-empty list of path operations that commit together as one logical commit, under one commit id that makes retries idempotent. A single-operation call is the one-element case. The first operation that fails aborts the whole request and names its position in `details.operation_index`.

get.description: Returns file bytes for the current revision at a path, or for a specific retained revision when `revision_no` is provided.

404.description: Namespace, path, or revision not found

503.description: The server is at its concurrent content-read limit; retry shortly

get.description: Lists a directory at the current namespace head.
Resolves the current path to a file inode and returns revisions for that file. If the file could be renamed, use the inode revision API for stable identity.
Returns the current metadata for a path, including inode identity, kind, display name, and file content metadata.

Returns the namespace's active deletions in ascending deleted-root inode order. Tombstone rows are retained forever, so entries never age out; each carries the inode id and deletion sequence undelete needs, plus the deleted name when the delete recorded one.

post.description: Creates a new namespace as a fork from the source namespace's current durable view.

Searches file content with a regular expression, accelerated by the namespace's grep index. Matches are verified against the real pattern and returned in ascending `(inode_id, byte_offset)` order; revisions committed after the index watermark are scanned exhaustively unless `allow_stale` skips them. Requires this deployment to serve grep and the namespace to carry a materialized steady-state grep root.

400.description: Invalid pattern, cursor, or an unindexable pattern without allow_scan

403.description: The backing store rejected its configured credentials

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: Grep serving is disabled, the grep index is not enabled, or its backfill has not completed on this namespace

503.description: The index trails the head past the scan budget

post.description: Starts an upload session for content that may later be attached to a file. Service-proxied uploads send bytes through the server; direct-put uploads return object-store presigned credentials.
Completes an upload session once the caller confirms the expected content reference. The response may include a short-lived validation token for a following file write.

put.description: Uploads bytes into a service-proxied upload session and returns the content reference for the stored object.

503.description: The server is at its concurrent proxied-upload limit; retry shortly

AbsolutePath.description: Validated complete absolute namespace path, serialized as a plain string.

ApiError.description: HTTP error body used by LoonFS APIs.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable reason from the [`ErrorCode`](crate::ErrorCode)
registry.

Carried as a string so clients keep working when a newer server
introduces a code they do not know; use
[`ErrorCode::parse`](crate::ErrorCode::parse) for typed access.

oneOf.description:
Structured context for the code, present when the failure carries
machine-usable identity (API spec, "Standard error contract"). Boxed
so the rare detailed error does not widen every error-carrying result.

feature.description:
For `not_supported` errors, the capability-document feature key the
client should reconcile against.

request_id.description:
Correlation id the server assigned to the failed request; the same
value is sent as the `x-request-id` response header.

AuthoritativePathEntry.description:
Authoritative metadata for one visible path.

This is the result shape for stat/list style reads. File entries include
revision and content summary fields; directory entries leave those empty.

absolute_path.description: Absolute path as rendered from stored display names.

committed_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock stamp of the commit that created the current revision,
for files; directories carry no modification time in v0.
Observational: `head_seq` and revision sequences are the order.

oneOf.description: Current content reference, for files.
Stored display name for this path component, absent for the nameless root.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence this answer was read from.

inode_id.description: Stable inode identity for this item.

inode_kind.description: Whether the item is a file or directory.

oneOf.description: Parent directory inode, or `None` for the root.
Current file revision number, for files.

size_bytes.description: Current file size in bytes, for files.

BeginUploadRequest.description: Request for starting an upload session.

oneOf.description: Required for `direct_put`; the server signs exactly this content object.
Requested upload transport. Absent keeps the existing service-proxied path.

BeginUploadResponse.description: Response for starting an upload session.

oneOf.description: Presigned write details for `DirectPut`, or `None` for `ServiceProxied`.

mode.description: Transport selected after applying server capability and request validation.

namespace_id.description: Namespace authorized to consume the eventual staged content.

upload_id.description: Durable session identity used by subsequent append and completion calls.

CapabilityDocument.description:
A deployment's self-description (API spec, "Capability discovery").

A remote client fetches this from `GET /v0/capabilities` and caches it; an
embedded engine exposes the same document as a constant. SDK gating logic
is therefore identical for both backends: check [`supports`] or
[`has_profile`], and treat a `not_supported` error as authoritative when
the two disagree.

[`supports`]: CapabilityDocument::supports
[`has_profile`]: CapabilityDocument::has_profile

features.description:
Named features and whether this deployment supports them. An absent
key means unsupported.

limits.description: Advisory numeric limits clients may use to pre-validate requests.

profiles.description:
Advertised profiles, each `plane/version`. All-or-nothing: every
required op of an advertised profile is implemented.

ChangeSeq.description:
Monotonically increasing namespace commit sequence number.

This is the global visibility order for a namespace.

after_seq.description: Exclusive cursor supplied by the caller, or the endpoint's initial position.

changes.description: Logical commits after `after_seq`, ordered by ascending namespace sequence.

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose ordered commit stream was read.

oneOf.description: Cursor to request when another page remains, or `None` at `through_seq`.

through_seq.description: Snapshot head through which this page was evaluated.

CheckpointId.description:
Durable checkpoint identifier.

A checkpoint is a durable bookmark to a namespace manifest version.

CommitId.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key for one logical commit.

Reuse the same `CommitId` when retrying the same request.

CommitRequest.description:
One commit: an idempotency key, an optional annotation, and an ordered
list of path operations that commit together (API spec, section 5.1).

A one-operation request is the one-element case of this shape, not a
different request: a convenience call and a batch produce the same commit
and the same fingerprint.

commit_id.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key for the whole request.

content_tokens.description:
Proofs for any new external content refs introduced by this request.
One proof covers every operation that names its content ref.

message.description:
Caller annotation recorded on the commit and reported by the change
feed. Part of the commit's identity: reusing `commit_id` with a
different message is a `commit_id_reuse_conflict`, exactly as it is
for an explicit commit.

operations.description:
Ordered operations to apply. Must be non-empty; they commit all
together or not at all.

CommitResponse.description:
Result of one commit.

Every commit resolves to this envelope — path-oriented operations and
explicit commits, embedded or remote. The commit id is the caller's
reconciliation handle: resubmitting the same request with the same id
replays this result instead of committing twice.

commit_id.description:
Idempotency key the commit landed under: caller-supplied, or
generated on the caller's behalf when the request carried none.

committed_seq.description: Sequence number where the commit became visible.

CommittedChange.description: One committed change in namespace order.

commit_id.description: Client idempotency key for this logical commit.

committed_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock stamp of the commit, in Unix milliseconds.
Observational: `seq` is the order.

events.description:
Semantic filesystem events, one per committed operation, in
request-operation order.

message.description: Caller annotation, omitted when absent and carrying no filesystem semantics.

seq.description: Namespace sequence for this logical commit.

CompleteUploadRequest.description: Request to complete an upload with the expected content ref.

content_ref.description: Content identity the caller expects the session to have staged.

CompleteUploadResponse.description: Response after an upload session is completed.

content_ref.description: Verified immutable content selected by the completed session.

namespace_id.description: Namespace that owns the completed session.

upload_id.description: Session whose result is now frozen for idempotent completion retries.

validated_content_token.description: Opaque server proof for a later commit, or `None` when the backend needs no token.

ContentRef.description:
Pointer to immutable file content.

A `ContentRef` is safe to publish only after the referenced bytes are
durable in the namespace's content store.

kind.description: Content strategy used by the referenced object.

size_bytes.description: Complete byte length of the referenced file content.

ContentStoreId.description:
Durable id for an immutable content store.

Content stores own file bytes. Namespaces point at content stores.

CreateCheckpointRequest.description: Request to create a durable checkpoint pin.

name.description:
Label recorded on the checkpoint record. A label, not a key: several
records may carry the same name over different bases.

ttl_ms.description:
Optional lifetime; the server computes the record's expiry from its
own clock. Absent means the pin holds until explicitly released.

oneOf.description: Manifest `metadata/root.json` references after the operation.

expires_at_ms.description: Expiry recorded on the record, when the request carried a `ttl_ms`.

DeleteDirectoryBehavior.description: Directory delete behavior for path-oriented deletes.

head_seq.description:
The head's last committed sequence; the delete linearized
immediately after it, so this is where history ended.

DestinationBehavior.description: Destination-conflict behavior for path-oriented puts, moves, and copies.

DirectPutUpload.description: Presigned direct_put upload details. The raw object key is intentionally not public.

access.description: Short-lived write capability the client uses without learning the raw object key.

content_ref.description: Exact immutable object identity and byte length covered by the signed request.

DisableGrepIndexResponse.description: Result of disabling the grep index on a namespace (admin plane).

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose grep root was disabled.

was_enabled.description: False when the namespace had no enabled grep root.

DisplayName.description: User-facing spelling of one path component.

EnableGrepIndexResponse.description: Result of enabling the grep index on a namespace (admin plane).

already_enabled.description: True when the namespace already carried an enabled grep root.

built_through_seq.description:
Sequence the index is built through when the enabling host reports
completion (an embedded host drives the backfill inside the call);
on a hosted server the backfill continues in its driver and this is
the sequence it targets.

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose grep root was enabled.

ErrorDetails.description:
Structured, machine-readable context accompanying an [`ApiError`].

Every field is optional: a code populates the fields that apply to it
(API spec, "Standard error contract"), and clients must tolerate absent
fields exactly as they tolerate unknown codes. Retry decisions still key
off the code; these fields carry the identity a caller needs to act —
which commit to resubmit, which epoch displaced it, which revision the
precondition saw.

active_acquired_at_ms.description:
Unix milliseconds at which the current epoch's acquirer took it, when
the head recorded one. Writer ids are process labels, so two runs on
one machine can share one; the stamp is what tells them apart.

oneOf.description: Deletion generation actually active for the inode.

active_writer.description:
Writer id recorded by the current epoch's acquirer, when the head
recorded one.

oneOf.description: Epoch that currently owns the namespace.
Revision that is actually current; absent when the inode has none.
Change-feed cursor the request asked to resume after.
Idempotency key of the commit the error concerns.
Revision the request expected to be current.
Epoch the failing writer session held when it was displaced.
Inode the failed precondition or operation targeted.

operation_index.description:
Position, in the request's operation list, of the operation that
failed. A commit applies all of its operations or none of them, so
this names the one that stopped the whole request.

oneOf.description: Deletion generation an undelete asked to recover.
Oldest sequence still promised for incremental replay.

committed_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock stamp of the commit that created this revision, in Unix
milliseconds. Observational: `committed_seq` is the order.

committed_seq.description: Namespace sequence that created this revision.

inode_id.description: File inode that owns this revision.

revision_no.description: Revision number within the file inode.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeCreated
oneOf.description: A file or directory was created.
Content of the first revision, for file creations.

name.description: User-facing spelling of the new entry.

parent_inode_id.description: Directory the new entry was bound under.

oneOf.description: First revision number, for file creations.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeContentChanged
oneOf.description:
A file received a new current revision — a put over an existing
file, or a revision restore (one durable fact for both).

content_ref.description: Immutable content published by the revision.

revision_no.description: New monotonic position in that file's revision history.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeMoved
oneOf.description: An inode moved to a new parent directory or name.

from_parent_inode_id.description: Directory that held the old binding.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeDeleted
oneOf.description:
A file or directory subtree was deleted. The enclosing change's
`seq` is the deletion generation an undelete request passes as
`deleted_at_seq`.

inode_id.description: Inode at the root of the deleted subtree.

oneOf.description: Spelling of the deleted binding, when the delete recorded one.

Directory that held the deleted binding, when the delete
recorded one.

oneOf.title: FilesystemChangeUndeleted
oneOf.description: A deleted inode was recovered and re-bound.

parent_inode_id.description: Directory the recovered entry was bound under.

FilesystemChange.description:
One semantic filesystem change inside a commit.

Each event corresponds to one operation of the committed request, in
request order. Events name inodes and their parent-directory bindings
rather than full paths; a consumer that needs paths can stat the inode
or maintain its own binding projection from this feed.

oneOf.title: FsOpCreateDirectory
oneOf.description: Create one directory.

parents.description:
Also create missing ancestor directories (the same auto-create
`put_file` performs). The final component must still be new.

path.description: Absolute destination path, rejected when invalid or already bound.

oneOf.title: FsOpPutFile
oneOf.description: Create or replace one file with an already-durable content ref.

behavior.description: Whether an existing file may receive a new revision instead of causing a conflict.

content_ref.description: Immutable bytes that must be covered by a valid preparation proof.

oneOf.description:
When set (with `replace` behavior), the put applies only while
the file's current revision is still this one; a raced write
fails the request instead of silently stacking on it, and a
missing file answers `path_not_found`.

path.description: Absolute destination path; missing ancestors are created automatically.

oneOf.title: FsOpDeletePath
oneOf.description: Delete one path.

behavior.description: Whether a non-empty directory may be tombstoned recursively.

oneOf.description:
When set, the delete applies only if the path still resolves to
this inode; a raced rebinding fails the request instead of
deleting (and reporting a recovery handle for) the wrong inode.

path.description: Absolute path that must resolve to a visible inode.

oneOf.title: FsOpMovePath
oneOf.description: Move one path to another path.

behavior.description: Whether an existing destination file may be replaced.

from_path.description: Absolute source path that must resolve to a visible inode.

to_path.description: Absolute destination whose parent must be visible and writable.

oneOf.title: FsOpCopyPath
oneOf.description: Copy one file path to another path.

behavior.description: Whether an existing destination file may receive a copied revision.

from_path.description: Absolute source path that must resolve to a visible file.

to_path.description: Absolute destination whose parent must be visible and writable.

oneOf.title: FsOpUndelete
oneOf.description:
Recover a deleted file or subtree: revoke the deletion of
`inode_id` recorded at `deleted_at_seq` (both reported by the
delete and by the change feed) and re-bind it at `path`. Answers
`not_deleted` when that generation is not the live one, so a stale
request never cancels a later delete.

deleted_at_seq.description: Observed deletion sequence, which prevents cancelling a newer tombstone generation.

inode_id.description: Deleted inode to make reachable again.

path.description: Absolute destination path whose parent must be visible and whose name must be absent.

oneOf.title: FsOpRestoreRevision
oneOf.description: Restore an older revision as the current revision for a path.

path.description: Absolute path that must resolve to a visible file.

source_revision_no.description: Existing historical revision whose content will be copied into a new current revision.

new_namespace_id.description: Durable namespace id for the fork target.

GcRequest.description:
Optional overrides for one garbage-collection pass. Absent fields use
the server's conservative defaults.

cursor.description:
Opaque resume token returned as `next_cursor` by an earlier pass
against the same namespace.

grace_window_ms.description:
Objects younger than this are never deleted, reachable or not. The
window has a derived safety floor (publication budgets plus provider
deadlines); a smaller value is rejected as `invalid_request`.

max_objects.description:
Maximum candidates examined by this invocation. Omit to retain the
run-to-completion behavior.

reap_window_ms.description:
Upload sessions older than this may be reaped. Must be at least the
grace window.

GcResponse.description: Result of one mark-and-sweep garbage-collection pass.

degraded_retention.description: True when ambiguous roots suppressed manifest/table deletion.

deleted_checkpoint_records.description: Released checkpoint records deleted after their grace window.

deleted_upload_sessions.description: Upload-session control objects deleted after the reap window.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque resume token when more candidates remain. Resuming rebuilds
every safety proof; the token carries enumeration position only and
is valid only against the same namespace.

released_expired_checkpoints.description:
Checkpoint records released because their expiry passed, or because
they sit on a terminally deleted namespace.

released_fork_checkpoints.description:
Fork-owned checkpoint records released because their target namespace
is provably gone.

released_missing_basis_checkpoints.description:
Active checkpoint records released because their basis manifest is
verifiably gone.

retained_candidates.description:
Candidates retained at delete time (grace window, missing
timestamps, or reachable from the fresh root set).

GrepGcResponse.description: Result of one explicit grep-index garbage-collection pass (admin plane).

deleted_other_objects.description: Other unreferenced grep objects deleted after the grace window.

deleted_segments.description: Unreferenced grep segments deleted after the grace window.

namespace_degraded.description: Whether unreadable namespace or grep state forced conservative retention.

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose grep-owned keyspace was inspected.

namespace_reaped.description: Whether an absent or tombstoned namespace had extension state reaped.

retained_candidates.description: Young or concurrently revived candidates retained by the pass.

absolute_path.description: The file's absolute path, derived at the snapshot.

byte_offset.description: Byte offset of the match within the file.

inode_id.description: Durable identity of the matched file.

line.description: The matching line, truncated to the server's line cap.

line_number.description: One-based line number of the match.

revision_no.description: The matched revision (the newest visible one at the snapshot).

allow_scan.description:
Permit a capped exhaustive scan when the pattern yields no required
grams. Refused beyond the server's scan budget.

allow_stale.description:
When the unindexed tail exceeds the scan budget, return
indexed-only results (reported via `tail_scanned: false`) instead
of failing with `index_lagging`.

case_insensitive.description:
Match case-insensitively. Verification is exact; the index remains
consulted through its case-folded grams.

cursor.description:
Resume cursor from a previous page. The cursor resumes strictly
after the last candidate the issuing page finished scanning and is
bound to that page's request; each page is evaluated against the
namespace head at page time.

oneOf.description:
Restrict matches to files under this complete absolute path, resolved
to a directory inode before candidates are filtered.

pattern.description:
The pattern, in the Rust `regex` crate's dialect (no backreferences
or lookaround). Patterns that require no literal bytes are rejected
with `query_unindexable` unless `allow_scan` is set.

built_through_seq.description: Commits at or below this sequence were answered from the index.

head_seq.description:
Sequence this page was evaluated at. Pages are evaluated against
the namespace head at page time; the cursor is an ordering resume,
not a snapshot pin.

matches.description:
Matches in ascending `(inode_id, byte_offset)` order. A page may
return fewer matches than its limit and still carry a cursor: the
per-page verified-candidate budget bounds how much content one
request reads, whatever the plan's false-positive rate.

tail_scanned.description:
True when revisions after `built_through_seq` were scanned
exhaustively; false only when `allow_stale` skipped them.

InodeId.description:
Numeric identity of a file or directory within a namespace.

Inodes are stable across renames.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence used for the read.

inode_id.description: File inode whose revisions were returned.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, if more revisions are available.

ListPathEntriesResponse.description:
One directory listing and the namespace head it was answered at.

The envelope names the listing target and head so an empty directory
still tells the caller which state it observed, and so the response can
grow without reshaping `entries`.

absolute_path.description: Absolute path of the listed directory.

entries.description:
Directory entries for this page.

Entries are returned in canonical name-key order. Higher-level display
surfaces may sort entries separately for presentation.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence this listing was read from.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, if more entries remain.

ListTrashResponse.description: One trash listing page: the namespace's recoverable deletions.

entries.description: Active deletions in ascending root-inode order.

head_seq.description: Head sequence this page was evaluated at.

MaintenanceStepKind.description:
One sub-step of a maintenance step, for callers that want to run exactly
one of them.

MaintenanceStepRequest.description:
Options for one explicit maintenance step. Absent fields use the
server's defaults; retention advance runs only when `retention` is true
and garbage collection only when `gc` is present.

oneOf.description:
Run the mark-and-sweep garbage collector after the step's
flush work. Nothing sweeps unless this is present.

max_wal_tail_segments.description:
Flush the visible WAL tail into metadata tables when it reaches this
many segments. Values above the write-rejection threshold are
rejected as `invalid_request`.

oneOf.description:
Restrict the step to one sub-step. Absent runs the whole step: WAL
flush, then reorganization, then retention if `retention` opted in,
then garbage collection if `gc` opted in.

retention.description:
Advance the retention floor to the flushed manifest head. Nothing
surrenders replay history unless this is true or `only` selects
`retention`.

MaintenanceStepResponse.description: Result of one explicit maintenance step.

oneOf.description: Garbage-collection report when the step opted into sweeping.

retention_floor_seq.description:
The retention floor after the step. Compare with
`status_before.retention_floor_seq` to see whether it moved.

status_before.description: Namespace status observed before the step acted.

ManifestId.description:
Monotonically increasing namespace manifest identity.

This is the durable file-set version identity for namespace manifests.
Initial/fork manifests may be seeded from the current head sequence, but
later manifest ids can advance for checkpoint metadata, compaction, or
fork/index metadata without a new namespace commit.

NameKey.description:
Name-policy-derived directory entry key.

Use this for exact name preconditions. Keep user-facing spelling in
`DisplayName`.

NamespaceId.description:
Durable id for one namespace.

A namespace is one filesystem history. This id is not a display name and
should not be reused after destruction.

NamespaceStatusResponse.description:
Status summary for one namespace.

This is the point-lookup answer to "does this namespace exist, and where
is its head?" — cheaper than listing all namespaces when only one matters.

oneOf.description: Current manifest pointer recorded by the head.

retention_floor_seq.description: Oldest sequence still promised for incremental replay.

wal_tail_segments.description: Number of visible WAL segments after the current manifest.

NamespaceSummary.description: Short namespace identifier returned by namespace create/fork operations.

oneOf.title: ObjectTransferAccessPresignedUrl
oneOf.description: Short-lived URL plus required headers for one object-store write.

headers.description: Headers that are covered by the signature and must be sent.

method.description: HTTP method the client must use.

ReleaseCheckpointResponse.description: Result of releasing a checkpoint pin.

was_active.description:
True when this call flipped an active record to released; false when
the record was already released or no longer exists. Release is
idempotent — the end state is the same either way.

ReorganizeStepOutcome.description:
What the metadata-reorganization part of a maintenance step did.

Deliberately coarse: the run counts and byte budgets a reorganization
consumes are engine policy, not a wire contract.

RevisionNo.description: Monotonically increasing file revision counter within one file inode.

TrashEntry.description:
One recoverable deletion: an active subtree tombstone plus the identity
of the binding it deleted, when the delete recorded one. Entries with no
recorded name predate the enriched tombstone rows; their inode and
sequence still form a complete `undelete` handle.

deleted_at_ms.description: Wall-clock stamp of the deleting commit. Observational.

deleted_at_seq.description: Commit sequence of the deletion; the other half of the handle.

oneOf.description: User-facing spelling of the deleted binding, when recorded.
Canonical key of the deleted binding, when recorded.
Directory that held the deleted binding, when recorded.

root_inode_id.description: Root inode the deletion hid; half of the recovery handle.

UploadContentResponse.description: Response after uploading bytes into a session.

content_ref.description: Digest and byte length computed from the accepted body.

namespace_id.description: Namespace that owns the upload session.

upload_id.description: Session into which the service staged these bytes.

UploadId.description: Durable id for one upload session.

ValidatedContentToken.description: Stateless proof that a LoonFS server already validated a content ref.

content_ref.description: Content identity the server attests it already verified.

token.description: Opaque, server-signed token. Clients must not parse it.

oneOf.description:
